Chief Musician
cheef myoo-ZISH-un
noun
Rendering the Hebrew lamnattsēach, from nātsach, “to oversee, to lead, to be preeminent, to set forward”; the appointed overseer and director of the temple song.

Biblical Definition

“To the chief Musician” stands at the head of fifty-five psalms, and once at the close of the prophet’s song, “To the chief singer on my stringed instruments” (Hab 3:19). The word is lamnattsēach, the one set to oversee, to lead, to set the work forward; for David did not leave the praise of God to chance, but appointed chief men over the Levites “to set forward the work of the house of the LORD” (compare 1Ch 23:4), with such as Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun over the courses of song. To the chief Musician a psalm was committed, that he might teach it to the singers, set it to its proper tune, and lead the whole congregation in ordered praise. He is the picture of office and order in worship: praise rendered not as each will, but under appointed oversight, decently and in its courses. And he is a shadow of a greater Leader of praise. For Christ Himself is the true Chief Musician, who stands in the midst of the congregation to lead His brethren’s song: “I will declare thy name unto my brethren, in the midst of the church will I sing praise unto thee” (Heb 2:12). The saints do not praise alone or unled; their great Forerunner raises the tune, and the redeemed lift their voices after Him.

Webster 1828 Definition

The appointed overseer and director of the temple song; a shadow of Christ, the true Leader of His people’s praise.

CHIEF MUSICIAN, the rendering of a Hebrew word meaning one set to oversee, lead, or set forward.

The direction “to the chief Musician” heads fifty-five psalms and closes the song of Habakkuk.

To him a psalm was committed, to teach the singers, set the tune, and lead the congregation.

He is the picture of office and order in worship, praise rendered under appointed oversight.

He is a shadow of Christ, the true Chief Musician who leads His brethren’s song.

Key Scripture

Psa 47, title — "To the chief Musician, A Psalm for the sons of Korah."

Hab 3:19 — "The LORD God is my strength, and he will make my feet like hinds’ feet, and he will make me to walk upon mine high places. To the chief singer on my stringed instruments."

1Ch 15:21 — "And Mattithiah, and Elipheleh, and Mikneiah, and Obededom, and Jeiel, and Azaziah, with harps on the Sheminith to excel."

Heb 2:12 — "Saying, I will declare thy name unto my brethren, in the midst of the church will I sing praise unto thee."

Modern Corruption

An office of ordered worship; it answers the modern distaste for appointed oversight in praise, and points to Christ the true Leader of His people’s song.

expand to see more

The office of the chief Musician faces no postmodern redefinition, but the order it represents is widely resented. The age prefers a worship without appointed oversight, where each does what is right in his own eyes and spontaneity is prized above the courses David set. The chief Musician rebukes this: the praise of God was committed to appointed men, taught, tuned, and led.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is leadership and order in worship, crowned by the leadership of Christ. As the chief Musician led the temple choir, so the Lord Jesus, the true Chief Musician, stands in the midst of the church to raise the tune of praise. The saints do not sing alone or unled; their great Forerunner leads, and the redeemed lift their voices after Him.

Hebrew Roots

Rendering the Hebrew for one set to oversee and lead, the Chief Musician directs the temple song and shadows Christ, the Leader of His people’s praise.

Chief Musician — Hebrew lamnattsēach, from nātsach, to oversee or lead.

The direction “to the chief Musician” heads fifty-five psalms.

Usage
